title: Neutrino: Fine-grained GPU Kernel Profiling via Programmable Probing
problem: Existing GPU profiling tools provide limited visibility into kernel execution details, hampering performance debugging and optimization
motivation: Fine-grained profiling is essential for understanding GPU kernel behavior, but current tools lack programmable/configurable profiling capabilities
method: Standard GPU profilers measure only a fixed set of metrics, limiting your ability to debug performance. This system lets you write custom measurement code and inject it directly into running GPU computations. Since your code runs during actual kernel execution, it captures exactly what you need to debug, without limitations of preset measurements. This programmable approach lets different users customize their profiling to specific performance questions.
key_novelty: It's the first GPU profiler to support programmable probing—letting you inject custom measurement code to observe what happens inside running computations.
contributions: Fine-grained profiling without requiring kernel source modification
baselines: Standard GPU profiling tools (NVIDIA nsys, nvprof, etc.)
limitations: Title-only paper; detailed metrics and comparison results unknown; overhead characteristics not specified
